qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Orphan drug exclusivities in oncology and neuroscience provide niche defensibility, but flagship blockbuster Somatuline faces ongoing generic lanreotide erosion while European health authorities enforce statutory price controls.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Specialty pharmaceutical model is heavily reliant on Somatuline, which faces accelerating generic competition in the US and Europe, while European single-payer price controls prevent sustained pricing power >= inflation.
qualitative.evidence: Somatuline historically accounted for over 35% of group revenue and the core of operating earnings, but its primary patents have expired and generic lanreotide alternatives have entered key markets. While Core Operating Margin remains ~32% and ROIC ~15%, the lack of volume-insulated pricing power against generic substitution and heavy reliance on external M&A (e.g. Albireo, Epizyme) fail the Munger moat durability standard.
